topics.definition: Normalization is the process of organizing data to reduce redundancy and improve data integrity.
topics.example: Split one large table into related tables.

topics.definition: 1NF ensures that every column contains atomic (indivisible) values and each row is unique.
topics.example: Store one phone number per row.

topics.definition: 2NF removes partial dependency by ensuring all non-key attributes depend on the whole primary key.
topics.example: Separate course details from student-course table.

topics.definition: 3NF removes transitive dependency so non-key attributes depend only on the primary key.
topics.example: Move department details to a separate table.

topics.definition: BCNF is a stronger version of 3NF where every determinant is a candidate key.
topics.syntax: Every determinant must be a candidate key

topics.definition: Normalization reduces redundancy, improves integrity and simplifies maintenance.
Denormalization combines tables to improve query performance.
topics.example: Join frequently accessed tables into one.

topics.definition: Normalization is used in banking, hospitals and college management systems.
topics.example: Separate Student, Course and Enrollment tables.
